questions.question: Distinguish between a cell and a battery. Explain why a D cell and an AA cell give the same voltage, and what voltage two cells connected in a row give.
questions.expected_answer: A cell is a single unit that transfers chemical energy to electrical energy, with positive and negative terminals; a battery is two or more cells connected together. Voltage depends on the chemicals in the cell, not its size, so alkaline D and AA cells both give about 1.5 V; the larger cell contains more chemicals and lasts longer. Two 1.5 V cells connected positive to negative give 1.5 + 1.5 = 3 V.

questions.question: Explain why copper is used for wires and why the wires are insulated. Describe what a resistor and a variable resistor do, and give a use for each.
questions.expected_answer: Copper is an excellent conductor, easily drawn into wire, flexible and resists corrosion. Insulation (PVC) prevents charge leaking out, prevents short circuits between wires and protects people from shocks. A resistor reduces the current in a circuit and transfers electrical energy into heat; uses: protecting an LED from too much current, or as a heating element in a kettle/toaster. A variable resistor (rheostat) has an adjustable resistance; uses: dimmer switch, volume control, fan or motor speed control.

questions.question: Draw (describe) the circuit diagram of two cells, a closed switch, a bulb and a fixed resistor connected in one loop. State four rules for drawing circuit diagrams and the direction of conventional current.
questions.expected_answer: Diagram: a rectangle with two cell symbols joined (long thin line positive, short thick line negative), a closed switch symbol, a circle with a cross (bulb) and a small rectangle (resistor), all in one loop connected by straight lines. Rules: use a ruler and straight lines; use right-angled corners (rectangular layout); use standard symbols; leave no gaps except in open switches; mark junctions with dots. Conventional current flows from the positive terminal of the battery around the circuit to the negative terminal (electrons flow the opposite way).
